item.title: Oxford Street bans traffic
item.description: London is pedestrianizing its version of Fifth Avenue. Cars, taxis, buses and even bicycles are now banned from Oxford Street.

item.title: How internet culture and franchise twists defined this year's horror movies
item.description: Horror critic and director Rebekah McKendry tells NPR's Juana Summers how internet culture led to some of this year's biggest horror movies, and shares some titles that may have gone under the radar.

item.title: Ebola outbreak tops 10,000 cases
item.description: The current outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the fastest spreading outbreak and it's not slowing down. What are the obstacles to getting it under control?

item.title: Some people with meat allergies from alpha-gal syndrome turn to exotic alternatives
item.description: People with alpha-gal syndrome can have allergic reactions to meat from mammals. Many of those affected change their diets to eat other proteins.

item.title: After a year of uncertainty, Job Corps is making a comeback
item.description: Last year, President Trump ordered more than 100 Job Corps training programs to close to save federal funds. A lawsuit stopped that, and now enrollment is up for "AI-proof" trade career training.

item.title: Democrats maintain momentum in race for Congress, per new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll
item.description: One week out from Election Day, Democrats continue to lead Republicans in the race for control of Congress, according to the latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll.

item.description: The highly anticipated, latest installment of Sarah J. Maas' romantasy series has hit the shelves. Hardcore fans were lined up (in their faerie ears) at the stroke of midnight.

item.title: Data centers are a hot-button issue for Ohioans as midterms near
item.description: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot-button issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

item.title: A group of former Freedom Riders is encouraging young voters in the South
item.description: A group of 1961 Freedom Riders is encouraging young people to vote across the South. Organizers stopped at Historically Black Colleges and Universities in time for election season.

item.title: Organ donation conversations are changing. Critics worry families may feel pressured
item.description: Transplant teams can talk to families about organ donation before they've decided whether to continue life-sustaining medical care for loved ones. Until now that's been forbidden.
